7. false-positive and alternative-explanation review cases;
8. provider/attestation outage and unsupported-platform behavior;
9. privacy/redaction/retention/export tests;
10. server evidence correlation and appeal/reversal audit flow where services are selected;
11. measurable startup, frame-time, memory, bandwidth, disk, and server-cost budgets;
12. proof that Disabled strips all protection-specific baggage;
13. release/update/rollback behavior across at least two signed versions;
14. hostile-input fuzzing and schema limits;
15. independent security review before any strong competitive-security claim.

No marketing claim such as “cheat-proof,” “unhackable,” or “military-grade” is permitted.


## Detailed Alluvium procedural-authoring contract


### Alluvium — product workflow and composition

#### Task-first normal authoring with graph/source underneath `ALLU-001` — *Normative*

The normal Alluvium experience is **task-first**, not graph-first. Users encounter procedural authoring through domain/task tools such as:

- Scatter Vegetation;
- Shape Terrain / Add Erosion Detail;
- Create Road / Path Network;
- Generate Rocks / Debris;
- Paint/Generate Biome Distribution;
- Build Ground-Cover Variation;
- Generate Environmental Set Dressing;
- Create Procedural Structure/Layout where a qualified first-party domain tool exists.

A task surface edits ordinary authoritative Alluvium recipe parameters and subgraphs; it is not a separate hidden generator. The same recipe can be opened as textual source, inspected as a graph when the visual graph exists, invoked headlessly, diffed semantically and reproduced in CI.

##### Beginner workflow

A representative first experience should be:

```text
Select terrain/region
-> Add Procedural Content
-> choose “Forest / Vegetation Scatter”
-> choose or accept sensible species/profile inputs
-> preview appears
-> manipulate density/exclusion/variation directly
-> manual edits are preserved as overrides
-> Build/Play uses the accepted result
```

The user should not need to understand fields, random substreams, graph evaluation, stable derivation IDs, cache classes or subsystem adapters before getting a useful result. Those concepts remain inspectable when needed.

##### Expert escape path

Every task surface must expose an obvious **Open Recipe / Open Graph / Inspect Generation** route. Advanced users can inspect:

- typed nodes and ports;
- shared fields;
- seed/substream lineage;
- representations/kernels;
- cache keys and dirty regions;
- generated IDs;
- override reconciliation;
- provenance/license flow;
- downstream Basalt/Penumbra/Cairn/NAV/etc. artifacts;
- execution cost and placement.

No task UI may become the only way to validate, migrate, bake or recover content.

##### UX acceptance

This decision inherits `PRODUCT-002`, `PRODUCT-005` and `APP-004`. A beginner should be able to create a useful procedural region without AI, external documentation or hidden terminal steps. An expert should be able to reveal and override every relevant generated decision without detaching from the ordinary project model.

#### Manual edits automatically become non-destructive overrides `ALLU-002` — *Normative*

When a user directly edits a generated object or supported generated property, Meridian interprets that action as curation rather than as an accidental violation of procedural ownership. The default is to create/update an explicit Alluvium override attached to stable generated identity.

Example:

```text
Generated tree 183
position = recipe result

user drags tree

Generated tree 183
position = recipe result + authored position override
```

The editor should present simple actions such as:

- **Keep Override**;
- **Return to Generated**;
- **Promote to Authored**;
- **Adjust Recipe Instead**;
- **Detach from Generation**.

These actions are normal typed editor transactions with undo, VCS attribution and source provenance.

##### Regeneration/reconciliation

After recipe changes, Alluvium attempts deterministic reconciliation against stable generated identity. Outcomes are typed rather than silently destructive:

```text
Applied
Migrated
Conflicted
Orphaned
Invalid
Detached
Promoted
```

If the recipe no longer creates the referenced object, the override becomes **Orphaned** and remains reviewable. Meridian may propose a retarget only when semantic evidence is strong enough; uncertain retargeting is never silently committed.

##### Bulk curation

Selection/bulk editing can produce compact override operations over stable sets/regions rather than millions of independent editor records where an equivalent semantic operation exists. The exact storage representation remains an implementation question.

#### Bake by default; bounded runtime-safe evaluation is explicit opt-in `ALLU-003` — *Normative*

The normal game ships **cooked outputs**, not a permanently live procedural graph runtime.

```text
.mproc / source inputs
-> Alluvium evaluation and bake
-> immutable/versioned generated artifacts
-> consuming subsystems publish their own runtime products
-> game ships those products
```

This applies naturally to authored/mostly-authored games and keeps startup, runtime footprint, determinism, failure surface and platform qualification simple.

##### Runtime procedural games

Projects may explicitly enable **runtime-safe recipes** for procedural games. A runtime recipe must declare and validate:

- allowed nodes/operations;
- CPU/GPU/memory/time budgets;
- determinism requirements;
- cancellation/fallback behavior;
- maximum output sizes/counts;
- source/save/network identity semantics;
- platform/web support;
- which receiving subsystem owns each published result.

Runtime evaluation cannot directly mutate private live subsystem state. It publishes typed candidate/generated artifacts or commands through the receiving authority’s normal publication path.

##### Zero-cost disabled requirement

If a product does not use runtime Alluvium, shipping must exclude its runtime evaluator, graph compiler, preview caches, runtime services/listeners, unnecessary node libraries and package data except narrow shared foundations already needed for cooked artifacts. This must be proven through dependency, binary-size, task/thread, memory and package audits.

#### Semantic stable generated identity with explicit ephemeral modes `ALLU-004` — *Normative*

Generated identity should remain stable across unrelated edits and reasonable recipe evolution. Identity is derived from durable semantic lineage rather than only from output position or serialized order. Candidate inputs include:

- stable recipe identity;
- stable node/subrecipe identity;
- explicit random substream identity;
- semantic generation path/category;
- stable source region/feature identity;
- local derivation identity chosen by the generator.

The exact hashing/derivation algorithm remains open, but the contract must support persistence, overrides, saves, VCS diffs, network references and downstream artifact attribution.

##### Ephemeral generation

Not every pebble or transient particle-like placement needs durable identity. Recipes can explicitly declare outputs/branches as **ephemeral**, allowing cheaper identity/rebuild behavior where persistence/curation is irrelevant. Ephemeral identity must not be used for objects later referenced by saves, gameplay, manual overrides or network authority without an explicit promotion/identity transition.

##### Identity drift

Major recipe edits produce a reconciliation report showing retained, new, removed, migrated and ambiguous generated identities. Silent mass reassignment of curated identities is a correctness failure.

#### Composable subrecipes and shared semantic fields `ALLU-005` — *Normative*

Alluvium should avoid both one enormous universal graph and a pile of disconnected per-subsystem recipes. Large procedural systems compose from smaller typed reusable recipes/subgraphs sharing explicit semantic fields/parameters.

Example:

```text
Forest Region
├─ terrain-shaping subrecipe
├─ moisture / drainage fields
├─ vegetation placement subrecipe
├─ ground-material subrecipe
├─ navigation hint/cost outputs
├─ acoustic-region outputs
└─ streaming/dependency metadata
```

A field such as moisture, slope, shelter or distance-to-road can be produced once and consumed by several domain adapters without creating hidden cross-adapter cycles.

##### Authority remains distributed

Composition does not turn Alluvium into the runtime owner of terrain, weather, physics, rendering, navigation, audio or vegetation simulation. Alluvium owns authoring/derivation and produces typed source/derived inputs. Consumers own runtime truth.

##### Reuse

Subrecipes can be packaged, parameterized, nested, versioned and semantically diffed. A project can replace or specialize one subrecipe without forking an entire world-generation graph.

#### World-first 1.0 product scope; broader general authoring experimental later `ALLU-006` — *Normative*

The underlying recipe/field/evaluation architecture remains deliberately **general enough** not to hard-code terrain/vegetation assumptions into the evaluator. However, the first-party product scope through the initial production era is **world/environment first**.

##### Current / 1.0 emphasis

First-party libraries, task tools and qualification prioritize:

- terrain/world shaping inputs;
- vegetation/ecological placement authoring;
- roads/paths/splines and infrastructure source;
- materials/ground-surface variation and weathering inputs;
- structures/environmental composition;
- fields, masks, exclusions and semantic regions;
- collision/navigation/acoustic/streaming source facets derived from the above;
- integration with Basalt, vegetation, Isobar, Torsant, Cairn, Penumbra, Wavefront, NAV, streaming, saves and build/cook.

This focus gives Alluvium a coherent high-value product surface instead of claiming that every asset type in Meridian has a mature procedural authoring library on day one.

##### Experimental later expansion

After the world-first system is mature, Meridian may expose **experimental general procedural-authoring domains** using the same core evaluator. Candidate areas include:

- Modeler/mesh/CAD document generation;
- generalized project asset generation;
- gameplay/world-logic placements;
- animation-support data;
- UI/content layout generation where a real use case exists;
- other typed domain adapters approved without creating a universal mega-graph.

Experimental expansion must prove a coherent task workflow, ownership boundary, source/recovery story, licensing/provenance behavior, performance and actual demand before graduating to a supported first-party product surface.

This decision narrows product promise, not architectural capability.

#### Adaptive, cancellable progressive live preview `ALLU-007` — *Normative*

Alluvium preview should feel immediate without pretending every world-scale recipe can fully regenerate synchronously. The preview scheduler adapts to cost and locality.

##### Cheap/local changes

Small parameter edits or local dirty regions update immediately where possible.

##### Expensive changes

For expensive edits the editor should:

1. identify and visualize affected regions/dependencies;
2. cancel stale queued/running preview work cooperatively;
3. retain the last-known-good accepted result;
4. prioritize selected/visible regions;
5. produce a coarse/partial preview quickly;
6. progressively refine quality/extent;
7. publish completed regions/results atomically;
8. explain remaining/stale work and estimated cost where sufficiently predictable.

Users can pause automatic preview, force a selected region, request full-quality preview or run an authoritative bake.

##### Failure behavior

A missing node library, worker crash, device loss, invalid parameter or failed output must not erase the previous valid preview or authored overrides. The recipe remains inspectable; stale products are clearly marked; recovery/retry uses the normal dependency graph.

##### Performance integration

Preview scheduling participates in the engine/editor task system and performance governor. It must not freeze MUI, audio preview, basic viewport navigation or editor input while background procedural work runs. GPU evaluation, when used, cannot starve interactive Penumbra rendering.

#### Cross-subsystem integration contract for Alluvium `ALLU-008` — *Normative*

Alluvium is one of the clearest tests of Meridian’s requirement that first-party subsystems work well together. The intended handoffs are automatic and typed:

| Consumer | Alluvium provides | Consumer retains authority over |
|---|---|---|
| Basalt | terrain recipes, splines, source fields, erosion/drainage/geometry inputs | runtime terrain geometry, precision, residency, deformation |
| Vegetation & Ecosystems | suitability/placement/growth-source inputs and generated identity | live populations, interaction, damage, growth/ecology |
| Isobar | climate/weathering/source fields, shelter/exposure inputs | live atmosphere, weather, wind, visibility, wetness |
| Torsant | initial conditions/material facets/baked inputs/runtime-safe generation inputs | live fire/fluid/smoke/thermal state |
| Cairn | collision/structural/physical-material source facets | live physics, contacts, constraints, destruction |
| Penumbra | geometry/material/volume/impostor/LOD/render metadata source | GPU resources, visibility, lighting, temporal presentation |
| Wavefront | acoustic materials/regions/portals/obstruction source | mixer, voices, live propagation/acoustics |
| NAV | walkability/routes/cost/exclusion source | runtime navigation representation, queries, agent traversal |
| Streaming | authored cells/bounds/dependencies/priorities | residency scheduling/activation/eviction |
| Save/gameplay | stable generated IDs, recipe instance identity, persisted parameters/override schema | gameplay/save authority and transactions |
| Asset/build | recipes/dependencies/provenance/cook requests | canonical asset/artifact/package identity and build transactions |

A normal world-authoring action should cause the required downstream rebuilds automatically. The user should not have to manually remember to regenerate terrain collision, then navigation, then acoustics, then HLOD, etc. The build graph explains exactly what changed and why.

#### Source/research basis and validation requirements

This contract is grounded in the retained Alluvium authority and the Unreal/Godot archaeology corpora. The research synthesis is:

- from **Godot**: preserve coherent authoring vocabulary, editor dogfooding, immediate feedback, source-linked tooling and generated baseline inspectors; avoid assuming one dynamic object/metadata substrate must also be the hot runtime representation or that a generic inspector is sufficient task UX;
- from **Unreal**: treat production tooling, asset transformation, observability and error/recovery as core engine infrastructure; test UX alongside backend architecture; learn from large-scale production pressure without copying mature-engine complexity and historical coupling;
- from **Alluvium v0.4**: preserve typed recipe/field evaluation, deterministic/reference paths, incremental/cache semantics, stable identity, non-destructive overrides, provenance/license flow, CLI/headless parity, runtime-authority boundaries and zero-cost baked-only shipping.

Required product/implementation evidence before broad production claims includes:

- novice task recordings proving useful generation without AI/docs/hidden terminal steps;
- expert inspection proving every automated decision is traceable and overridable;
- source/graph/task round-trip tests;
- stable generated-identity and override-reconciliation fixtures across unrelated and structural edits;
- clean/dirty preview and bake latency distributions;
- cancellation and last-known-good recovery under invalid source/worker crash/device loss;
- deterministic reference-vs-optimized differential tests;
- exact downstream invalidation explanations across Basalt/Penumbra/Cairn/NAV/Wavefront/etc.;
- provenance/license propagation and cooker rejection tests;
- baked-only zero-runtime-cost proof;
- web/server/platform qualification for any runtime-safe recipe profile that claims support.

The Alluvium product architecture is complete for this specification. Remaining details are implementation or research work unless evidence exposes a genuine product contradiction, including:

- exact canonical `.mproc` encoding;
- evaluator IR and kernel portfolio;
- exact field representations;
- CPU/SIMD/GPU placement algorithms;
- stable-ID derivation/hash implementation;
- override storage/reconciliation algorithms;
- runtime-safe node allowlists/budget schema;
- precise preview scheduling heuristics;
- exact visual graph interaction design;
- domain-specific generation algorithms and libraries;
- experimental post-1.0 general-domain graduation criteria.

---


## Detailed Isobar and Camellia environment contract


### Weather Profile / World Environment is the normal authoring surface `ISO-001` — *Normative*

Ordinary weather authoring uses a clean, task-oriented Weather surface inside the already-adopted World Environment workspace. A developer can set or select condition, intensity, wind, visibility, temperature and transition behavior without understanding weather fields, cloud-density data structures or simulation clocks. Local Weather, Timeline and Advanced/Fields are progressive disclosure paths, not prerequisites.

The editor may use presets/templates internally, but the resulting weather remains real editable project state. A profile is not an opaque generated blob. Beginner workflow must work without AI or documentation, consistent with `APP-004` and the Unreal/Godot UX evidence already recorded.

### Directed / Guided / Simulated authored-intent modes; Guided default `ISO-002` — *Normative*

Weather intent supports at least three semantic control modes:

- **Directed** — authored beats/constraints are hard requirements; useful for cinematics, narrative beats, competitive readability and scripted events.
- **Guided — DEFAULT** — the author provides targets/ranges/constraints; Isobar chooses coherent fronts, cloud evolution, precipitation, local response and transition detail within those bounds.
- **Simulated** — authored initial conditions/forcing/climate constraints are provided and Isobar evolves the system with the largest qualified degree of freedom.

Modes may be selected per world/region/transition rather than forcing one project-wide philosophy. Switching mode is an explicit authoring transaction with preview and determinism/save implications.

### Rich common Field contract with representation portfolio `ISO-003` — *Normative*

The public Isobar field semantics do not freeze one storage/simulation topology. The **production baseline** remains sparse regular tiled/hierarchical data because it is straightforward to stream, budget, batch and accelerate, but Isobar must remain rich and highly customizable. Behind the same typed field/query contracts, qualified implementations may include:

- sparse regular tile pyramids / clipmap-style pages;
- adaptive tiles/bricks;
- analytic far/weather regions;
- variable-resolution or unstructured research representations;
- GPU-specialized dense/local grids;
- baked/precomputed fields;
- project extension representations that satisfy publication/query/diagnostic contracts.

The representation planner/governor selects products by scale, active influence, quality target, hardware, latency, determinism, memory and downstream needs. Developers can pin or author constraints, but do not ordinarily tune tile topology manually.

**Rich simulation is a product requirement, not a promise that every point in the world is always simulated at maximum resolution.** Meridian reaches richness through hierarchical/adaptive fidelity and promotion of important regions.

### Low/zero-configuration procedural weather is first-class `ISO-006` — *Normative*

Isobar must support games that do not want to hand-author weather. A project can choose something equivalent to:

```text
Weather: Automatic / Procedural
Climate: Automatic
Seed: Automatic or explicit
```

and receive believable evolving weather using the same real Isobar state, not a disconnected canned visual randomizer.

Automatic procedural weather should:

- use world/environment/biome/climate metadata when available;
- otherwise use a safe neutral first-party climate/profile rather than demanding setup;
- generate regional transitions, fronts/storm probabilities, cloud/wind/precipitation and local consequences coherently;
- cooperate automatically with Camellia time/season state when enabled;
- remain seedable, inspectable, saveable/networkable under the selected determinism contract;
- allow the developer to take control at any time by switching a region/event to Guided or Directed;
- expose high-level style/climate controls for games that want customization without field editing.

This is a core manifestation of Meridian's product goal: powerful simulation should **reduce** setup work rather than require every game to become a weather-engine project.

### Camellia owns shared world time and optional celestial state `CAM-001` — *Normative*

The shared service proposed in v0.33 is named **Camellia**. It remains deliberately smaller than Isobar or other named simulation authorities.

Camellia owns canonical typed world-time state and may provide optional calendar and celestial/ephemeris products. Typical consumers include:

```text
Camellia
├─ Isobar      solar/seasonal forcing and procedural climate schedules
├─ Penumbra    sun/moon/sky orientation and presentation inputs
├─ Bearings    schedules/time-aware behavior
├─ gameplay    clocks, schedules and events
├─ vegetation  season/growth timing
└─ Wavefront   time-aware ambience/music conditions
```

A project that only needs `elapsed world time` does not pay for astronomical/calendar machinery. Exact calendar models, time zones, leap rules, moon/planet ephemerides and fictional-calendar authoring remain follow-up product decisions.

### One logical atmosphere; finest active representation is local truth `ISO-007` — *Normative*

Isobar owns **one logical atmospheric/weather state** whose runtime representation changes automatically with relevance, target capability, numerical need, gameplay significance, and quality budget. The public/product model must not expose the historical planning shorthand “B weather” and “C weather” as separate systems.

Conceptually:

```text
Climate / durable regional state
        -> Reduced Atmosphere
        -> refined Reduced field pages
        -> Resolved Atmosphere domains
        -> optional hero/research refinement
```

Where a qualified Resolved Atmosphere domain is active, its local resolved thermodynamic/flow/cloud state is the **finest active truth** for quantities it owns. Consumers that need less detail receive derived/restricted views; they do not independently run contradictory local wind/cloud state.

Where no Resolved domain exists, Reduced Atmosphere is fully authoritative for that region and continues the same logical weather through a cheaper model. Promotion and demotion change representation, not weather identity.

#### Promotion contract

Promotion is automatic-first and transactional:

1. detect predicted visual/gameplay/physical benefit under `PRODUCT-006`;
2. select a qualified resolved representation/solver for platform, budget, determinism, and requested quality;
3. snapshot Reduced state plus boundary conditions and source provenance;
4. reconstruct unresolved fine state from deterministic substreams, cached history, procedural spectra, neighboring domains, or solver-specific initialization;
5. prewarm/converge while the prior accepted representation remains live;
6. validate boundary continuity, units, epochs, conservation/error expectations, and downstream authority;
7. atomically publish the Resolved domain at a safe epoch;
8. allow consumers to migrate to richer views without manual game glue.

The developer may pin, prefer, forbid, or inspect a fidelity choice. They should not normally place or tune simulation LOD regions manually.

#### Demotion contract

Demotion conservatively restricts Resolved state back into Reduced state. The exact retained quantities depend on the selected algorithm, but the contract may include:

- integrated water/condensate/precipitation reservoirs;
- filtered velocity/momentum and wind tendencies;
- temperature/humidity/pressure-like summaries;
- cloud layer/cell topology, phase, development/dissipation state;
- storm/front identity, motion, severity, and precipitation tendency;
- authored constraints and gameplay-visible events;
- uncertainty/conservation/restriction error;
- deterministic reconstruction metadata where required.

Fine-scale state that has no semantic/persistence consequence may be discarded under the project's persistence/determinism contract.

### Selective fine-to-coarse feedback `ISO-008` — *Normative*

Resolved domains may influence regional Reduced evolution, but **not every fine perturbation feeds back**. Feedback occurs when a declared bounded criterion determines that resolved behavior materially changes larger-scale weather.

Examples that may justify feedback:

- a strongly resolved storm updraft changes condensate/precipitation tendencies;
- a resolved front interaction materially changes storm motion/intensity;
- large thermal forcing changes a region's atmospheric tendency;
- a gameplay-scale event intentionally models enough energy/mass exchange to influence regional weather.

Examples normally kept local:

- turbulence around one building;
- wake around one vehicle;
- a small ventilation fan;
- decorative cloud microstructure;
- high-frequency eddies whose aggregate effect is below the configured threshold.

Feedback uses typed exchange terms, declared cadence/latency, bounded influence, provenance, and stability diagnostics. A hidden per-frame cyclic dependency is forbidden.

### Reduced Atmosphere is still rich weather simulation `ISO-009` — *Normative*

“Reduced” means **lower numerical/spatial/temporal fidelity**, not “fake” or “cosmetic.” A world can run entirely on Reduced Atmosphere and still receive production-quality procedural weather.

Reduced evolution may model/represent:

- regional pressure/temperature/humidity-like fields;
- fronts and storm/cell identities;
- large-scale wind/advection;
- cloud layers and condensate summaries;
- precipitation initiation/intensity/type;
- local shelter/topography/canopy response at available resolution;
- day/night and Camellia forcing;
- climate/season/biome inputs;
- wetness/snow/ice source state through existing Isobar/Torsant handoffs;
- procedural stochastic detail using explicit substreams;
- authored Directed/Guided constraints.

A developer selecting `Weather: Automatic` can ship a believable evolving-weather game without ever activating high-resolution atmospheric fluid simulation.

### Criticality-aware atmospheric persistence `ISO-010` — *Normative*

The save/network system persists **meaning**, not indiscriminately every simulation voxel.

For normal **Stable** projects, persist at least:

- durable Reduced weather state and region/storm/front identity;
- Camellia/world-time linkage;
- authored intent/constraints;
- deterministic seeds/substreams and solver/version provenance needed for reconstruction;
- important accumulations/handoffs;
- selective Resolved checkpoints/history when the microstate itself affects gameplay, continuity, persistence, or a developer-declared authored requirement.

Decorative cloud turbulence can usually reconstruct after load. A persistent tornado whose exact local state is affecting bodies, damage, fire spread, networking, or replay may require a checkpoint or stronger replayable state.

For **Deterministic** projects, each selected Isobar algorithm must document whether equivalent resolved state can be regenerated from durable state/history or whether resolved checkpoints are required. Strict Determinism certification fails if the active authoritative weather portfolio cannot satisfy the declared envelope.

### Global determinism UX simplification `DET-001` — *Normative*

Meridian exposes two ordinary determinism choices:

```text
Stable         <- default
Deterministic  <- explicit stronger guarantee
```

**Stable** is not “fast/nondeterministic.” Meridian still uses explicit RNG streams, stable IDs/order where practical, reproducible traces, controlled publication epochs, and avoids gratuitous schedule-dependent behavior. Performance engineering targets Stable first.

**Deterministic** activates the stronger documented envelope required for lockstep, exact/qualified replay, deterministic simulation testing, or projects that choose stronger reproducibility. It may restrict algorithms, GPU paths, concurrency, floating-point choices, or adaptive techniques when qualification requires it.

**Strict Determinism** is a project/build validation policy, not another runtime mode. It asks the cooker/validator to reject the build/profile if any gameplay-authoritative enabled system falls outside the requested deterministic envelope.

The old generic `Fast / Stable / Deterministic / Strict` four-choice UX is superseded. Subsystems can still publish more precise internal capability/evidence labels, but those are not four ordinary project buttons.

### Camellia capability depth `CAM-002` — *Normative*

Camellia is the focused shared world-time/celestial service.

Always-available minimal core:

- monotonic/world time representation;
- time scale and pause/advance semantics;
- simulation/presentation-safe time snapshots;
- source/save/network identity needed by consumers.

First-party capabilities automatically included only when consumed:

- calendar/date systems;
- day/year cycles;
- seasons;
- solar position/ephemeris;
- lunar state;
- broader celestial/astronomical calculations;
- project-defined calendar adapters where appropriate.

This is capability stripping, not user setup. If an Isobar climate profile requests seasonality or Penumbra requests physically meaningful solar movement, Meridian resolves the needed Camellia capability automatically and explains the dependency.

### Simple Weather surface + advanced Atmosphere/Simulation workspace `ISO-011` — *Normative*

Ordinary users work primarily in:

```text
World Environment
  -> Weather
```

The default surface emphasizes semantic intent: Automatic/Directed/Guided/Simulated, condition/profile, precipitation, cloud character, wind character, visibility, temperature, transition timing, local overrides, and timeline access where relevant.

A dedicated **Atmosphere / Simulation** workspace exposes expert controls without polluting the default workflow:

- Reduced/Resolved field visualization;
- region/front/storm/cell inspection;
- resolved-domain bounds/residency/fidelity;
- cloud condensate/density/velocity/thermodynamic fields;
- high-detail flow state and boundaries;
- promotion/demotion and feedback evidence;
- algorithm/representation ID and capability profile;
- solver stability and conservation/error diagnostics;
- CPU/GPU/memory/transfer cost;
- platform/web fallback comparison;
- deterministic reconstruction/persistence state;
- trace/timeline inspection;
- authored pin/prefer/forbid overrides.

Both views use one source/command/transaction model. Opening the advanced workspace never “detaches” the weather into a separate expert configuration unless the developer explicitly creates a specialized custom implementation.

### Isobar automatic-optimization contract — DEEPENED

Isobar is a flagship consumer of `PRODUCT-006`. The developer supplies artistic/gameplay requirements and platform budgets; the engine owns routine tuning.

Automatic decisions may include:

- spatial and temporal field resolution;
- Reduced versus Resolved promotion;
- solver update cadence/substeps;
- cloud/flow representation;
- CPU/SIMD/GPU execution;
- active-domain movement/resize/prewarming;
- sparse-block allocation;
- atmospheric rendering source quality supplied to Penumbra;
- history/checkpoint frequency;
- interpolation and local refinement;
- far-field analytic/surrogate use;
- memory/VRAM residency;
- web/mobile/native downgrade products.

The governor must optimize **jointly with Penumbra, Torsant, vegetation, Cairn, Wavefront, NAV/Bearings, world streaming, networking and saves** where their costs depend on the same weather state. It is not acceptable for each subsystem to independently choose a locally optimal fidelity that multiplies total cost or creates contradictory environment state.

Every automatic compromise is inspectable. Gameplay correctness, authored constraints and declared deterministic guarantees outrank frame-budget recovery.

### Isobar integration closure matrix

| Neighbor | Isobar relationship after this round |
|---|---|
| Penumbra | Isobar owns atmosphere/weather meaning; Penumbra owns visual representation, lighting, volume residency, temporal reconstruction and compositing. Resolved atmospheric fields may be consumed directly through renderer-owned products. |
| Cairn | Isobar publishes wind/environment/material influence semantics; Cairn decides mechanical body response. High-detail resolved flow can provide a richer sampled velocity field without becoming the rigid-body solver. |
| Wavefront | Same weather snapshot drives ambience, shelter, impacts and acoustic parameters; no private audio weather RNG. |
| Basalt | Basalt supplies terrain/topography/shelter/drainage geometry facets; Isobar owns atmospheric evolution and coarse surface environment state. |
| Torsant | Isobar supplies precipitation, wind, moisture and coarse accumulation; detailed fluids/fire/thermal state transfers through typed single-owner contracts. |
| Alluvium | Alluvium authors climate/weather/exposure inputs and recipes; Isobar owns live weather state. |
| Vegetation/Ecosystems | Isobar supplies climate, wind, moisture, precipitation and season forcing; vegetation runtime owns plant/population response. |
| Artus | Artus may consume environmental wind/temperature/precipitation semantics for body performance; Isobar never owns character animation. |
| NAV/Bearings | Isobar produces visibility/weather/environment facts and cost inputs; NAV/Bearings own traversal/planning interpretation. |
| Meridian UI/editor | World Environment gives simple semantic controls; advanced Atmosphere/Simulation gives full technical visibility over the same transactions. |
| Camellia | Camellia supplies time/calendar/season/celestial state requested by Isobar; Isobar remains weather authority. |
| Networking/saves | Durable semantic/coarse state and critical resolved checkpoints use stable IDs/epochs and declared deterministic envelopes. |
| Build/platform/web | Cooker strips unused capabilities and selects qualified field/solver/render products; disabled weather has zero recurring/runtime/package baggage under existing capability rules. |
| Diagnostics/Ponder | Trace connects authored weather -> field evolution -> fidelity choice -> consumer effect -> cost/fallback/recovery and can explain “why did this weather/quality change?” |


## Detailed Torsant simulation contract


### Production Torsant belongs in Meridian 1.0 `TOR-001` — *Normative*

Torsant is optional **per project**, but Meridian 1.0 must qualify a useful production-grade first-party simulation portfolio rather than shipping only contracts for later plugins. The production floor targets at least coherent fire/smoke, thermal state and heat propagation, broad surface/shallow water, localized detailed liquid interaction, steam/boiling hooks, wetness/suppression, and automatic integration with the rest of the environment stack.

This does **not** require every research solver or every experimental chemistry capability before 1.0. Torsant's production floor is capability-scoped and zero-cost when unused. A project such as The Shape of Down can omit it entirely where appropriate.

Acceptance must be based on representative visible/gameplay evidence, not solver demos in isolation. A feature is not production-qualified merely because a fluid box runs. It must survive authoring, streaming, save/load, networking where applicable, downgrade, recovery, web/native profile handling, editor iteration and cross-subsystem use.

### Effect-first semantic authoring `TOR-002` — *Normative*

Normal creators work in terms of intent:

```text
Make Flammable
Add Fire
Add Water
Add Flow Source
Add Drain
Add Heat Source
Freezeable
Boilable
Smoke Source
```

Meridian constructs and maintains required Torsant domains, fields, boundaries, source/sink data, caches and solver products underneath. Solver-domain plumbing is an expert surface, not a prerequisite for adding a campfire or water flow.

Task-specific panels remain deliberately designed rather than exposing raw generated schema inspectors as the entire UX. Advanced views expose exact field state, representation, solver, stability, source provenance, resolution, budgets and manual overrides.

### Multiresolution finest-useful-representation simulation `TOR-003` — *Normative*

Torsant adopts the same broad *representation principle* as Isobar without forcing the same numerical solver. Each physical domain may have multiple qualified representations:

```text
semantic / analytic state
    <-> coarse field or shallow model
    <-> detailed local solver
    <-> specialized hero/research representation
```

The finest active qualified representation owns the local physical state it actually resolves. Promotion reconstructs/refines state from the coarser representation, validates continuity and publishes atomically. Demotion conservatively summarizes the state required for gameplay, persistence and subsequent refinement.

Different effects may use different algorithms. This is explicitly **not** a universal-fluid-solver mandate.

### Rich game combustion by default; deep combustion experimental `TOR-004` — *Normative*

The production/default Torsant combustion model is rich enough to support convincing game simulation through semantic material state such as:

- ignition response and thresholds;
- available fuel and depletion;
- burn-rate behavior;
- heat release and transfer;
- smoke/soot/char tendency;
- moisture and suppression response;
- spread class/directionality;
- consumed/charred/remnant state;
- coupling to Isobar wind/rain, vegetation, Cairn structural damage, Penumbra media/light, Wavefront audio and gameplay rules.

It is **not marketed as engineering-certified combustion chemistry**.

A separate first-party **Experimental Deep Combustion** toggle/capability *(working label; exact public name open)* may pursue substantially richer oxygen availability, combustion products, chemistry-like species, buoyant reactive flow, radiative/convective heat transfer, fuel mixtures and related research. It is deliberately allowed—not rejected—but it must stay out of the normal authoring complexity and create zero baggage when disabled. Promotion into the production/default path requires measured visual/gameplay value, stability, performance, maintainability and clear semantics.

### Automatic specialized liquid portfolio `TOR-005` — *Normative*

No single liquid algorithm becomes the Meridian public model. Torsant may automatically compose/select representations such as:

```text
large calm water / oceans       -> analytic/render-coupled surface semantics
runoff / rivers / floods        -> shallow-water / terrain-coupled fields
interactive local free surface  -> qualified FLIP/APIC/MPM/SPH-like or successor solver
spray / droplets / foam         -> particles / derived detail
viscous or granular special case-> specialized solver when justified
```

The developer declares required behavior and artistic/gameplay constraints. Meridian's performance governor decides solver/representation, domain resolution, substeps, particle density, GPU/CPU path, meshing/detail and downgrade whenever it can do so without changing required semantics. Experts can pin or replace those choices.

### First-class practical phase/material transitions; generalized matter experimental `TOR-006` — *Normative*

The normal production system supports coherent practical transitions including:

```text
dry <-> wet
water <-> ice
water <-> steam
cold <-> hot
unignited -> burning -> charred/consumed
selected solid <-> molten transitions where a qualified material/profile uses them
```

Authority remains distributed: Isobar owns atmosphere/coarse environment forcing; Torsant owns detailed local thermal/fluid/phase state; Basalt owns durable terrain geometry; Cairn owns mechanical truth; vegetation owns living plant state; gameplay owns project-specific meaning. Typed handoffs prevent duplicate ownership.

A separate **Experimental Matter/Chemistry** capability *(working label; exact UI/name open)* may explore a much more generalized material-transformation/chemistry system. This possibility is intentionally retained. It is not a default 1.0 complexity burden and must be zero-cost/zero-baggage when disabled. Its eventual product status is evidence-gated.

### One source across preview, bake/cache and runtime `TOR-007` — *Normative*

An authored Torsant effect/material/environment definition can compile/evaluate into several execution products without becoming separate unrelated asset types:

```text
interactive preview
high-quality editor simulation
reusable cache / baked result
runtime live simulation
cheap shipping surrogate
server-authoritative semantic state
web/mobile reduced product
```

Meridian normally recommends or automatically selects among them from gameplay requirements, determinism, target hardware, frame/memory budgets and artistic constraints. A developer can force a mode. Switching from live to baked/cached should not require re-authoring the effect.

Caches/bakes remain derived and reproducible where promised; source authority and provenance survive. Expensive simulation jobs are cancellable/resumable and show progress, expected resource use and stale-dependency state.

### Torsant automatic-optimization and cross-subsystem contract

`TOR-001`–`TOR-007` deepen `PRODUCT-006`: Torsant should aggressively remove routine simulation optimization work from the developer. Automatic decisions include domain creation, sparse residency, representation promotion/demotion, solver/update resolution, substeps/iterations, collision detail, CPU/SIMD/GPU placement, render-source detail, cache/bake strategy, persistence detail and target-specific fallback.

Relevant first-party handoffs must work without glue code:

| Neighbor | Automatic Torsant relationship |
|---|---|
| Isobar | wind/humidity/rain forcing; suppression; surface-fluid ownership; steam/moisture feedback only through stable typed seams |
| Basalt | terrain boundaries, drainage, containment, erosion/material-operation requests; no direct source mutation |
| Alluvium | initial conditions/material facets/generation/cook/bake authoring; no runtime authority theft |
| Penumbra | smoke/steam/flame/heat-haze/liquid source products; Penumbra retains rendering/temporal/residency authority |
| Cairn | solid boundaries, body interaction, buoyancy/forces where qualified, destruction/structural response |
| Wavefront | semantic combustion/fluid/impact/boil/steam/acoustic events and environment parameters |
| Vegetation | moisture, burning, heat/damage and persistent ecosystem consequences through vegetation-owned state |
| NAV/Bearings | traversal/hazard/cost/visibility consequences through typed semantic fields/events |
| Artus | body/environment response inputs where meaningful; no direct pose ownership |
| Saves/networking | stable semantic/coarse state plus only required resolved checkpoints/authority data |
| Camellia | time scale/world time/season inputs when the effect depends on them |
| Gameplay | game-specific consequences, permissions and objectives remain game authority |

### Torsant implementation research and evidence — *Open implementation research*

Still open under `RG-TOR-001` and implementation research:

- exact gas/fire/smoke solver portfolio and combustion approximations;
- sparse-grid/block/page representation;
- exact liquid algorithms by workload;
- pressure solve, advection, surface reconstruction, foam/spray and viscosity policies;
- thermal conduction/convection/radiation approximations and coupling rates;
- phase-boundary numerical treatment;
- promotion/restriction conservation tolerances;
- solver stability/downgrade thresholds;
- GPU/WebGPU/Metal/Vulkan/D3D12/CPU paths;
- device-loss and server/headless fallbacks;
- deterministic qualification and replay;
- save/network encodings;
- bake/cache formats and resumption;
- exact experimental deep-combustion/generalized-matter scope;
- cross-effect two-way feedback stability;
- benchmarks against Niagara Fluids, NVIDIA Flow, Salva/Nexus/Slosh and independent Meridian prototypes;
- PEN-B07/PEN-B14/PEN-B15 plus new water/fire/phase-transition workloads.

## Detailed editor interaction and workspace contract


### Curated task workspaces with optional freeform customization `EDUX-001` — *Normative*

Meridian's normal editor shell is organized around **curated task workspaces**. A new user receives strong first-party layouts for major activities rather than an empty docking canvas or a giant one-size-fits-all screen. Candidate workspace families include World, 2D, Code, UI, Animation, Audio, Modeling, Debug/Profile and other domain-specific surfaces that prove necessary. Exact names/count are not frozen by this lock.

A workspace is a presentation/configuration layer over the same project/documents/commands; switching workspace does not create a second copy of world state or change source authority.

Normal expectations:

- the default layout for each workspace is excellent enough that most users never customize it;
- the primary task, selection, project/assets, properties and relevant diagnostics remain easy to find;
- common vocabulary and keyboard behavior remain stable across workspaces;
- workspaces may add/remove/rearrange specialized tools without turning every task into a new application;
- the editor remembers personal workspace state where useful.

Experts may dock, split, float, move across monitors and save variants under `EDUX-004`. Customization is optional power, never prerequisite setup.

Qualification must include a clean-profile novice path: open Meridian for the first time and perform the core game-creation loop without first rearranging the shell.

### Baseline schema Inspector plus deliberate task interfaces `EDUX-002` — *Normative*

Every schema-exposed editable object receives a functional generated Inspector. Important high-frequency or semantically complex workflows may layer purpose-built interfaces over the same typed properties/commands. Neither surface becomes a second authority.

Generated property metadata may describe:

- human label and category/group;
- type, units and legal range;
- enum/asset/entity/reference picker semantics;
- authoring-only/runtime meaning;
- default/revert value and source;
- validation and warning rules;
- performance/cost hints where meaningful;
- ownership/subsystem provenance;
- multi-edit behavior;
- advanced/rare classification;
- documentation/help anchor.

The ordinary Inspector should prioritize what people actually need. Rare implementation details collapse under Advanced/Technical sections or task-specific views. Experts can search/reveal the complete legal property surface. Favorites, recent changes, reset/revert and multi-selection editing are leading requirements.

Task panels never perform private mutation: edits issue the same typed transactions as the Inspector, `.mui`, commands, code APIs or later AI. This preserves undo, source maps, collaboration and validation.

### Universal ultra-fast launcher / command-discovery surface `EDUX-003` — *Normative*

Meridian provides one global launcher/quick-input surface capable of searching several typed scopes while dedicated local searches remain available. Candidate result families:

```text
Commands
Assets
Entities
Files / source documents
Settings
Open documents
Tools / workspaces
Recent/relevant items
Later extension-provided legal scopes
```

A result is typed, not a label/stringly action. Commands resolve to the central command registry. Assets use stable asset IDs/catalog data. Entities carry authoring/runtime identity appropriate to the active context. Settings resolve through the typed settings schema. Files/source results use project/document indexes.

The query syntax may support light scope prefixes/filters, but discoverability must not depend on memorizing punctuation. Contextual ranking may consider active workspace, selection, recent use, exact prefix/word boundaries and user history without making globally valid commands disappear mysteriously.

Menus, toolbars, shortcuts, contextual actions, command search, automation/CLI where legal and later AI should converge on the same underlying commands rather than independently implementing behavior.

#### Search/index architecture `EDUX-006` — *Normative product direction*

This surface must be **F.A.S.T.** Meridian treats search latency as part of editor interaction latency, not as an indexing utility that is allowed to hitch the UI.

Architecture direction:

```text
Authoritative project/world/asset/settings/command changes
        ↓ incremental typed change streams
Scope-specific compact indexes
        ↓ immutable/versioned query snapshots
fast candidate generation
        ↓ fuzzy/exact/context ranking
merged top-K result stream
        ↓
Universal Launcher
```

Rules:

1. **Command lane** is memory resident after registration; filtering does not touch disk.
2. **Asset lane** consumes the Central Asset Catalog/index rather than scanning source folders per query.
3. **Entity lane** consumes editor/world semantic indexes and working-set snapshots rather than walking every entity.
4. **File/document lane** maintains a compact path/name index; content search may invoke a separate indexed/direct-search pipeline.
5. **Settings lane** is generated from the typed settings registry.
6. Index updates are incremental and may be processed concurrently/background; they must not block pointer/keyboard/viewport rendering.
7. Result lanes can stream independently. A very fast command/exact result can appear before a slower project-search lane finishes.
8. Index generations/freshness are tracked. If a result might be stale, invoking it revalidates stable identity before mutation.
9. Missing/corrupt indexes degrade gracefully to partial results/direct bounded search and rebuild asynchronously; they do not freeze the entire editor.
10. `.meridianignore`/project source policy feeds indexing semantics where appropriate; ignored build/cache/vendor/generated content is not accidentally made expensive by every search.

Initial **qualification targets**, deliberately subject to representative-corpus calibration:

- warm launcher opening/presentation should fit inside the normal next interactive frame rather than visibly spawning late;
- warm in-memory command matching/ranking targets a sub-frame p95 budget compatible with 120 Hz interaction;
- warm indexed file/asset/entity/settings scopes should surface useful top results in roughly the tens-of-milliseconds class, not hundreds, on the primary baseline machine and representative large projects;
- typing must remain responsive while slower lanes continue;
- million-item stress corpora and pathological near-match queries are required before claiming scale;
- index update storms/imports/branch changes receive explicit backpressure/prioritization tests.

The normative performance spec will freeze exact numerical thresholds only after benchmarking equivalent corpora. The product requirement—**querying should feel instant**—is locked now.

#### Current implementation-donor/research notes

- VS Code demonstrates one quick-input surface with command/file/symbol modes and fuzzy matching, reinforcing the unified-launcher UX pattern.
- Zed similarly provides a command palette plus project/file/symbol search and context-sensitive action visibility.
- `ripgrep` is a strong permissive Rust reference/dependency candidate for direct text-search fallback because it is optimized for recursive source search and ignore semantics; it is not the universal metadata index.
- `nucleo` is an important high-performance fuzzy-picker benchmark/reference because its managed worker streams candidates and publishes snapshots without blocking the UI, but its MPL-2.0 license means Meridian's permissive-first policy should not source-mine it. Dependency use would require an explicit policy decision.
- MIT `skim`/`fuzzy-matcher`, other permissive matchers, and a Meridian-owned matcher/index specialized for typed editor objects remain prototype candidates.

The final search architecture is chosen through benchmark quality, latency, memory, Unicode behavior, incremental-update cost, license/provenance and maintenance—not by library popularity.

### Deep layout customization with excellent recovery `EDUX-004` — *Normative*

After the curated default, advanced users may:

- split/dock/reorder tabs/panels;
- float panels/windows;
- move surfaces between monitors;
- duplicate compatible views;
- save named personal workspace variants;
- temporarily maximize/focus a view;
- use multiple project/editor windows where the multi-window contract permits;
- restore first-party defaults at any time.

Layout state is personal/user state by default, not project source and not something a repository silently imposes on collaborators. Projects/extensions may provide **recommended** layouts/workspaces through an explicit opt-in/import flow.

Recovery is mandatory:

- Reset Current Workspace;
- Restore First-Party Default;
- undo/recover recent layout operations where practical;
- corrupted/incompatible persisted layout falls back safely;
- missing extension panels produce placeholders/recovery rather than destroying the layout;
- monitor removal/DPI changes rehome inaccessible windows automatically.

No layout file may corrupt project content.

### Stable transform fundamentals plus contextual direct manipulation `EDUX-005` — *Normative*

Meridian keeps a small, predictable direct-manipulation core—Select, Move, Rotate, Scale and domain equivalents—while surfacing specialized controls contextually. The goal is less toolbar hunting without “magic” gestures the user cannot discover.

Examples:

- select light → radius/cone/area handles;
- select audio region → resize/falloff handles;
- select spline → knots/tangents/add/split actions;
- select physics constraint → anchors/limits;
- select UI element → bounds/anchors/alignment;
- select Artus contact → semantic contact targets;
- select NAV link → endpoints/requirements;
- select Alluvium field/region → relevant brush/extent controls.

Contextual controls obey the same command/transaction system. Their discoverable alternatives appear in the universal launcher and/or local context menu. The editor can show concise shortcut/tool hints when a new tool becomes active without permanently filling the viewport with overlays.

An optional pointer-local favorites/marking/radial interaction may be prototyped, especially for Modeler/CAD and pen/tablet workflows, but no essential command may exist only there.

### Integration consequences

The five locks imply cross-engine contracts:

- **MUI:** docking, virtualized lists, quick-input surfaces, semantic accessibility, task panels, nine-slice, high-refresh input and rich direct-manipulation overlays are production workloads.
- **Penumbra:** editor surfaces/viewports and MUI display lists need cheap partial redraw, overlay composition, multi-window surfaces and GPU profiling.
- **Asset system:** the Central Asset Catalog must expose fast versioned discovery/index snapshots and change streams.
- **Authoring graph/world:** entity/outliner indexes and selection identities feed the launcher and contextual inspector without duplicating source authority.
- **Source control:** command/layout/project actions remain semantic and recoverable; personal layout data does not pollute repository diffs by default.
- **Ponder:** help anchors attach to commands/properties/tools and are discoverable through the same launcher.
- **Extensions:** extension panels/commands register typed metadata and cannot create private command palettes.
- **AI later:** the future harness consumes the same commands/indexes/semantic selection state; AI is not required to make them useful.
- **Accessibility:** launcher result types, ranking state, contextual tools and workspace layout must have semantic/keyboard/screen-reader paths.

### Validation additions

Permanent editor UX workloads should include:

- 10k/100k/1M command-like candidate fuzzy-match synthetic corpora;
- 1M-file/asset-name stress indexes with incremental rename/add/remove storms;
- huge scene/world entity index with unloaded/streamed working sets;
- cold/missing/corrupt index recovery while the user keeps editing;
- branch/checkpoint transition causing widespread index invalidation;
- keyboard-only universal launcher workflow;
- screen-reader announcement and result-type semantics;
- layout restoration after monitor unplug and extension removal;
- nine-slice visual goldens across DPI, scaling, stretch/tile modes, atlas regions and tiny target rectangles;
- repeated nine-slice batching/geometry-cost benchmark;
- direct manipulation round trips through undo/redo/source transactions.

Editor search traces should distinguish index update time, candidate-generation time, ranking time, cross-lane merge time, UI presentation latency, memory footprint and stale-result revalidation. A generic “search took 50 ms” counter is not sufficient.


### Hybrid physical-source + semantic asset organization `EDUX-007` — *Normative*

Meridian's Project/Asset Browser exposes **source truth and semantic organization at the same time**.

The normal model is:

```text
Project Sources
├── Characters/
├── Materials/
├── Audio/
└── ...

Collections
├── Main Character
├── Forest Assets
└── Demo Content

Smart Views
├── Recently Used
├── Favorites
├── Used In Current Scene
├── Missing References
├── Large/Expensive Assets
├── Modified / Uncommitted
└── Validation Problems
```

Rules:

- physical/source location remains visible and honest; Meridian does not pretend tags are filesystem paths;
- collections/tags are non-owning semantic organization and may reference the same asset many times without duplication;
- typed catalog queries can filter by asset kind, source/provenance, usage, dependency, size/cost, platform readiness, validation state, source-control state and project-defined facets;
- list/grid/detail/reference/dependency views consume the same Central Asset Catalog identities;
- rename/move is a semantic source transaction that updates stable references instead of creating hidden redirector debt;
- "show in source", "show dependents", "show dependencies", "find usages", "why included in build?" and "why missing?" remain one-click/launcher-accessible operations;
- huge catalogs are virtualized/indexed and never synchronously enumerated to render a browser panel.

`EDUX-006`'s ultra-fast launcher and the browser use shared catalog/index infrastructure rather than private duplicate indexes.

### Meridian-first keymap with maintained familiarity presets `EDUX-008` — *Normative*

Meridian has one canonical, documented **Meridian Default** keymap. The command system—not raw key events—is source authority for editor actions.

A small maintained familiarity set may approximate high-value muscle memory from major tools such as Blender, Unity, Unreal and Godot where mappings are semantically safe. Presets never rename Meridian concepts, hide commands or fork editor behavior.

Users may:

- bind/rebind any exposed command;
- assign multiple bindings where legal;
- use chords/sequences;
- define contextual bindings with inspectable scope;
- import/export personal mappings;
- create favorites/local menus;
- search commands by action name, old/current shortcut or category.

Conflict resolution is explicit. Meridian shows both conflicting commands, scope and suggested remedies. The universal launcher always displays the active shortcut, so documentation can name actions rather than assume one physical layout.

Keyboard layout, platform modifier conventions, accessibility input and text-entry conflicts receive real tests. Keymaps are user state by default; a project may recommend mappings only through an explicit opt-in profile.

### One project session, many windows; many sessions without ambiguous authority `EDUX-009` — *Normative*

A **Project Session** is the unit that owns open project/editor service state. A session may present many top-level windows across many monitors:

```text
Project Session
├── Window 1 — World
├── Window 2 — Code + Debug
├── Window 3 — Material / Assets
└── Window 4 — Play / Profiler
```

Several projects may be open at once, but they remain distinct sessions rather than casually mixing repositories, source-control operations, builds or Play state in one ambiguous shell.

Session restoration may preserve, where safe:

- projects and session identities;
- workspace/layout variants;
- top-level window positions/sizes/monitor assignment;
- open source/assets/documents;
- tab groups;
- selection and viewport position;
- relevant profiler/debug tabs;
- unsaved source transactions/recovery state;
- resumable background jobs.

Restoration does not blindly resurrect stale runtime handles. Source/runtime generations are revalidated, missing assets/panels become explicit placeholders, removed monitors trigger safe rehoming, and corrupted session state falls back without damaging project source.

### One typed Activity/Job system with contextual progress `EDUX-010` — *Normative*

Every substantial asynchronous editor/build operation implements a common typed **Job/Operation** contract instead of inventing a private spinner.

Representative operations include import/reimport, shader compilation, asset cooking, Alluvium evaluation, Torsant bake/simulation, indexing, source synchronization, builds, tests, packaging, downloads, cache repair and platform submission.

A job records at least:

```text
identity
owner/source
state
current stage
progress or indeterminate reason
dependencies
start/elapsed time
resource/budget attribution
cancelability
pause/resume/retry support where legal
outputs/artifacts
diagnostics/logs
failure and recovery action
```

One global **Activity** surface can inspect all work, but progress also appears contextually at its origin. Clicking either representation resolves to the same job identity.

Design rules:

- ordinary background jobs stay quiet;
- decisions/failures requiring attention escalate;
- modal "please wait" UI is reserved for genuine exclusive-state transitions;
- cancellation is cooperative, safe and explicit about what remains valid;
- stale jobs caused by source changes are marked/restarted/rebased according to the owning graph rather than silently publishing obsolete results;
- large jobs expose enough stage/resource information to answer "what is Meridian doing?" and "why is this slow?";
- notification spam is avoided by grouping related child jobs.

This job contract is shared with CLI/headless/CI where semantics match.

### Ponder-backed contextual learning; self-explanatory UI remains the first line `EDUX-011` — *Normative*

Meridian must be learnable without AI and without requiring external documentation for ordinary workflows.

The hierarchy is:

1. **The UI itself explains the normal action.**
2. Contextual labels/tooltips/empty states/validation explain the immediate concept.
3. **Ponder** can provide "What is this?", "Show me how", "Why is this disabled?", examples, deeper reference and optional walkthroughs.
4. External/reference documentation remains available for expert depth.

Ponder-backed walkthroughs operate against the real editor and detect completed semantic actions rather than playing a disconnected slideshow. They may teach first 2D/3D game, UI, multiplayer, profiling, importing, packaging and similar workflows. They are resumable/abandonable and never become a gate.

Hard rule: if a common operation is only discoverable because Ponder tells the user a hidden shortcut/menu path, that is an editor UX defect to fix.

### Editor UX qualification gate

The professional editor UX contract is complete for this specification, subject to implementation and qualification evidence.

Before production qualification, Meridian must still demonstrate:

- novice core loop without docs/AI/terminal;
- expert override/inspection without fighting automation;
- low-latency command/index behavior at large scale;
- keyboard, screen-reader, text scaling and high-DPI behavior;
- multi-monitor/session recovery;
- unified background activity/cancellation;
- physical/semantic asset browsing on large projects;
- layout/keymap recovery;
- clean stripping of editor-only data from runtime products;
- user studies that explicitly compare workflow friction with Unity, Unreal, Godot and relevant DCC/IDE tools.

The exact `.mui` language grammar, AST/source-preservation syntax and implementation data structures remain separate.

---



#### Accepted Ahead-of-Time editor product decisions `ED-AOT-001..005` — *Normative*

The editor is sufficiently planned to implement. The following owner-level choices close the remaining pre-implementation editor product questions.

##### Moderate professional density `ED-AOT-001`

Meridian's default editor density is **moderately dense and clean**, not ultra-dense and not spacious/SaaS-like.

Required consequences:

- trees, tables, tabs, asset rows and code-adjacent surfaces remain compact;
- Inspector/task controls receive enough breathing room for clarity and accessibility;
- decorative whitespace is minimized;
- the primary viewport, code editor, graph, model, timeline or other work surface receives the majority of available area;
- progressive disclosure hides rare/technical state instead of solving clutter with oversized spacing;
- optional Compact and Comfortable user density variants MAY exist, but the first-party default remains Moderate.

Exact row heights, padding, line heights and control metrics are evidence-selected rather than product ABI.

##### Persistent top workspace strip `ED-AOT-002`

Major curated workspaces use a **persistent top workspace strip** as the normal navigation model.

Representative concept:

```text
World   2D   Code   UI   Model   Animate   Audio   Profile
```

Only relevant/enabled workspaces need appear by default. Overflow, reordering, search and responsive collapse are allowed. The Universal Launcher and menus remain alternative access paths, but launcher-only navigation and a permanent icon-only left activity rail are not the default workspace authority.

##### Three-column World workspace with viewport priority `ED-AOT-003`

The default World workspace uses:

```text
left: Scene / Assets / Project
center: primary World viewport
right: Inspector / contextual task properties
bottom: optional Activity / Problems / Console / Profiler drawer
```

The viewport is aggressively prioritized. Secondary docks collapse or become drawers before the primary work surface becomes unusable. Deep user customization remains available through the general workspace/layout contract.

##### Contextual and pinnable Meridian AI `ED-AOT-004`

When AI is enabled, normal discovery uses contextual typed actions such as **Ask**, **Plan**, **Explain** and **Fix** through the launcher, diagnostics, context menus, selected-object actions and relevant workspaces.

A normal AI/Task surface may be docked or pinned by users who want persistent access. Meridian does not require a permanently dominant AI sidebar, glowing global AI button or mandatory dedicated AI workspace. When AI is disabled, empty AI chrome is absent.

##### Vision architecture now; qualification later `ED-AOT-005`

The first-party Meridian-specialized model/tool architecture supports visual inputs from the beginning, but first-party vision does **not** block the first public local-model release.

A first release may qualify through excellent structured/textual Meridian understanding: source, schemas, scenes, selections, commands, diagnostics, profiler data, logs, runtime incidents, tests and semantic state.

Vision is a separate capability/qualification lane for screenshots, frame captures, viewport regions, UI imagery, plots, graphs, reference imagery and visual-artifact diagnosis. This decision does not authorize AI-generated game assets and does not pull the deferred reconstruction program into 1.0.

#### Ahead-of-Time Meridian Editor visual and interaction target `EDUX-VIS-001..010`

**Status:** normative visual/interaction direction refining the canonical editor UX contract; exact numeric theme/geometry tokens remain evidence-tunable. This section fills the exact visual-design gap that the canonical specification intentionally left prototype-gated. It does not weaken accessibility, user testing, or evidence gates. Exact pixels, metrics, and colors may move when real rendering/accessibility evidence proves a better value, but the visual character and hierarchy below are the target.

#### Editor visual thesis

Meridian should look like a serious piece of professional creative software that happens to be pleasant to use.

It should **not** look like:

- a web dashboard wrapped in a native shell;
- a game launcher;
- a neon "gamer" interface;
- a card-heavy SaaS product;
- a copy of Unreal, Blender, Unity, Godot, VS Code, Zed, Fusion, or Inventor;
- a wall of collapsible property groups;
- an AI application with sparkles everywhere;
- a flat gray prototype whose only defense is "developers don't care about appearance."

The visual character is:

- calm;
- precise;
- content-first;
- fully designed neutral dark and light themes, with initial selection following explicit user/system policy rather than becoming project source;
- moderate professional density without crowding;
- mostly flat, with depth communicated by tonal separation and one-pixel boundaries rather than giant shadows;
- restrained in color;
- crisp at high DPI;
- responsive at high refresh rates;
- readable for long sessions;
- visibly native to Meridian.

The canvas, code, model, graph, timeline, waveform, profiler, or world being edited should always visually outrank the editor chrome.

#### Design language

##### Surfaces

Use a small tonal hierarchy rather than "cards inside cards":

1. **Canvas/background** — deepest neutral.
2. **Primary dock surface** — slightly elevated neutral.
3. **Interactive/selected surface** — small tonal lift or accent edge.
4. **Transient surface** — menu, launcher, popup, tooltip; stronger contrast and subtle elevation.
5. **Modal/exclusive surface** — rare, strongly separated and used only when an operation truly requires exclusive attention.

Avoid:

- glassmorphism;
- background blur as a structural requirement;
- giant rounded containers;
- decorative gradients;
- fake 3D bevels;
- excessive drop shadows;
- colored panel backgrounds by subsystem.

##### Shape

- Base corner radius: restrained, approximately 4–6 logical px on ordinary controls.
- Dense tabular/code/tree surfaces may use square or nearly-square geometry.
- Larger floating menus/dialogs may use approximately 8 px radii.
- Do not put every panel inside another rounded rectangle.
- Separators are generally 1 logical px and low contrast.
- Selected/focused states use an accent edge/outline, not a large glow.
- Split handles remain easy to grab even when their visible separator is thin.

##### Typography

Preferred functional UI face: **Atkinson Hyperlegible Next**, provided real rendering, localization, metric, licensing, and density tests remain favorable.

Technical/code face: **JetBrains Mono** or another qualified high-legibility monospace with comparable metrics.

Hierarchy target:

- ordinary UI: ~13–14 logical px;
- compact secondary metadata: ~11–12 logical px;
- panel section headers: ~12–13 logical px semibold;
- prominent empty-state/title text: ~16–20 logical px;
- code: independently configurable, normally ~13–15 logical px.

Typography must remain sharp rather than over-antialiased/blurry, and scaling is semantic rather than a screenshot zoom.

##### Color

Dark-theme prototype direction (the Light and High-Contrast themes require independent qualification):

```text
canvas/background     near-black neutral, not pure black
dock/panel            slightly lighter neutral
raised/transient      one further tonal step
primary text          near-white neutral
secondary text        cool-neutral mid/high gray
muted text            lower-contrast gray
selection/accent      one restrained cool accent
error                 red family
warning               amber family
success               green family
information           blue/cyan family
```

A reasonable prototype palette may begin around:

```text
canvas      #111316
panel       #171A1F
raised      #1D2127
border      #2A3038
text        #E7EAF0
secondary   #AAB1BC
muted       #727B88
accent      #66A3FF
error       #FF6675
warning     #E6B450
success     #69C68C
```

These exact values are **prototype seeds, not eternal ABI**.

Rules:

- Accent color is a theme/user preference, not subsystem identity.
- Error/warning/success colors retain semantic meaning and cannot be repurposed for decoration.
- Do not assign every Meridian subsystem a loud branded color.
- Selection remains understandable in monochrome/high-contrast modes.
- Light theme is designed independently, not produced by mechanically inverting dark theme.
- High-contrast mode is first-class.

#### Permanent shell

The shell uses **one calm application frame plus workspace-local toolbars**, not a giant permanent toolbar containing the whole engine.

Conceptual default:

```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Project ▸ Scene        World  2D  Code  UI  Model  Animate  Audio  Profile      ▶ Play  Build ⌕ │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ context/tool strip: Select | Move | Rotate | Scale | Snap | View | local tool controls          │
├───────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┤
│               │                                                       │                         │
│ Scene/Assets  │                                                       │ Inspector               │
│ Project       │                 PRIMARY WORK SURFACE                  │                         │
│ Collections   │             viewport / editor / graph / etc.          │ properties              │
│               │                                                       │ task-specific controls  │
│               │                                                       │ source / revert / help  │
├───────────────┴───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┤
│ optional contextual drawer: Activity | Problems | Console | Timeline | Profiler | Tasks          │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ source/change state    target/profile    diagnostics count       jobs       frame/perf/context  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

##### Top application strip

Prototype target height: approximately 38–42 logical px; final metrics are evidence-selected.

Left:

- project/session name;
- current primary document/world breadcrumb;
- source/change-state affordance when useful.

Center:

- curated workspace tabs;
- tabs can scroll/overflow rather than compress into unreadability;
- only relevant/enabled workspaces appear by default;
- a project can enable more without making every project display every subsystem.

Right:

- Play/Stop;
- active Play/product target;
- Build;
- universal launcher/search;
- Activity attention state;
- optional user/provider state when a capability genuinely needs it.

AI does **not** receive a permanently glowing global button. When enabled, AI tasks are opened through commands, context actions, a task view, or an explicitly pinned panel.

##### Workspace-local context/tool strip

Prototype target height: approximately 30–34 logical px; final metrics are evidence-selected.

It owns only the current workspace/tool context. Examples:

- World: Select/Move/Rotate/Scale, snapping, coordinate space, viewport mode.
- Code: symbol/breadcrumb navigation, run/debug configuration, split/navigation actions.
- UI: select/container/text tools, responsive preview, state/variant preview.
- Model/CAD: sketch/feature/selection mode and constraints relevant to active mode.
- Animation: key/pose/contact tools and preview controls.

Do not replicate global project actions here.

##### Bottom status strip

Prototype target height: approximately 22–24 logical px; final metrics are evidence-selected.

Use it for quiet, high-value state:

- source/change state;
- errors/warnings;
- current build/product target;
- background job count/state;
- active frame/performance profile where relevant;
- contextual selection/tool hints;
- cursor/symbol location in Code;
- transform/grid state when useful.

Do not turn it into an advertisement strip.

#### Default dock geometry

On a typical desktop screen:

- left navigation/source dock: ~260–320 px;
- right Inspector/task dock: ~320–400 px;
- bottom drawer when open: ~180–300 px;
- primary canvas gets every remaining pixel.

These are defaults, not hard limits.

Minimum-window behavior prioritizes the primary work surface. Docks collapse into drawers/tabs before the canvas becomes useless.

#### Panel anatomy

Every panel should have:

```text
title / identity
optional search/filter
small number of high-frequency actions
content
optional footer/status only when genuinely useful
```

Panel headers are quiet and compact. Avoid nested header bars unless there is a real second scope.

Tabs use a restrained active underline/edge or tonal selection. Inactive tabs should remain readable without all competing equally for attention.

#### Inspector

The Inspector is one of Meridian's most important surfaces.

Default structure:

```text
Selected identity
type / source / stable identity summary
high-value warnings if present

Transform / primary task properties
-----------------------------------
Common properties
Context-specific authored controls

Advanced
Technical
Generated / provenance / runtime details

Revert / source / explain / docs
```

Rules:

- Common properties appear before implementation details.
- Search filters the whole legal property surface.
- Advanced groups are collapsed by default.
- Properties modified from their inherited/default source receive a small, obvious revert/source indicator.
- Multi-selection shows shared values, mixed states, and safe multi-edit behavior.
- Warnings appear adjacent to the value that caused them.
- Units are visible and editable naturally.
- Expensive/quality-affecting properties may show a subtle cost hint, not a scary badge wall.
- Purpose-built task interfaces reuse the same typed property/command authority.

#### Scene / hierarchy / asset browser
